To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the suppression of microbiota endotoxemia by NK46 alleviates gut dysbiosis, inflammation, and cognitive decline in 2 Alzheimer’s disease models, 5XFAD-transgenic and aged mice.

oral administration of NK46, a probiotic isolated from human gut microbiome, can alleviate gut dysbioses and cognitive decline in aged and Alzheimer’s disease model mice via the suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammation.
oral administration of B. longum NK46 alleviated gut dysbiosis, LPS production, cognitive decline, and amyloid- β accumulation in the hippocampal region of 5XFADA-Tg and aged C57BL/6 mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential use of NK46 as a probiotic for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
the potential use of NK46 to treat Alzheimer’s disease via microbiota-gut–brain axis.
the potential of NK46 as a therapeutic agent in the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the administration of NK46 can simultaneously alleviate gut dysbiasis and cognitive decline via the microbiota LPS-NF-κB axis in 5XFADA-Tg and aged mouse models.
NK46 treatment alleviated cognitive decline through the modulation of microbiota LIP-mediated NF-κβ signaling in the brain of 5XFADD mice.
the suppression of the gut dysbiosis with NK46 alleviates cognitive decline through the modulation of the microbiota-gene-brain axis in 5XFDA-Tg and aged mouse models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppression of NF-κB signaling in the brain by NK46 treatment is associated with the alleviation of gut dysbioses in Tg and aged mice.
NK46 treatment can alleviate cognitive decline in 2 mouse models of Alzheimer’s disease by suppressing gut dysbiosis, LPS production, NF-κB signaling, and neuroinflammation.

the gut dysbiosis in 5XFDA-Tg and aged mouse models is associated with cognitive decline, and this can be alleviated by the oral administration of B. longum NK46, a probiotic strain isolated from healthy human gut microbiota.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gut microbiota is involved in the progression of cognitive impairment in Alzheimer’s disease and that modulation of gut dysbioses by probiotics may be a promising therapeutic approach to alleviate cognitive impairment in patients with Alzheimer’s disease.

gut dysbiosis is a key player in the pathogenesis of cognitive decline in 3xTg-AD and aged mice, and that gut dysbios is an important target for therapeutic strategies to prevent cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease.
the gut microbiota can be a therapeutic target to alleviate cognitive decline via the modulation of the microbiota-gene-brain axis.
